title.narrative: Skill Up! Unlocking success: Empowering vulnerable youth for sustainable perspectives in Nepal

description.narrative: Overall Objective: The economic stability and decent income generation of vulnerable young people have improved through profitable employment or self-employment, resulting in increased food and nutrition security.Outcome (Project Objective):Young vulnerable people use the acquired (labour) market relevant competencies and the provided access to necessary resources & labour market linkages to secure (self-) employment opportunities.

The main group of participants (target group) for the program are disadvantaged and highly vulnerable youths (gender balanced) between 15 and 35 years from rural, semi-rural and urban settlements whose prospects to become employed or to work as self-employed entrepreneurs shall sustainably improve by the provision of job-related theoretical and practical skills and life skills. These include above all people from fragile contexts, with challenging living conditions, such as people who are severely affected by poverty and hunger, early school dropouts, young (single) mothers, migrants, people with disabilities and so on. At the same time the program address (non-) formal institutions, companies, and other training providers (including facilitators and trainers), in the field of vocational education and training. They will benefit through qualification training (for training enterprises) and through cooperation and involvement in the development of curricula and networks to build up on the recognition of the non-formal TVET sector. Furthermore, young micro-enterprises are targeted in order to improve their performance on the labour market.Direct Participants:Skill development training including incubation for 1080 unemployed youths aged 16-35 years (50% female).Indirect project participants: households = 3000

The second phase of the program will build on the achievements of the first phase and aims to ensure that disadvantaged young people are employed or self-employed and earn a decent income for themselves and their families. It emphasizes incubation, skill provision, SME development and policy advocacy. Enhancing the capacity of green vocational schools, emerges as a critical component, serving as a hub for training, creating standardized green skill curricula and facilitating market access for trained entrepreneurs. This project will highlight the necessity of bridging gaps in skill development ecosystems among the unemployed youth, providing comprehensive support from pre-training strategies to post-training support, including mentorship, market linkages, and business planning.
